model.title: Temporary support and payment of advances regarding the increased fertiliser prices due to the Middle East crisis

summary.lead: Official summary (Legislative Observatory, Decision by Parliament, 1st reading):

blocks.text: The European Parliament adopted by 576 votes to 62, with 15 abstentions, a legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 as regards a specific type of intervention to provide exceptional temporary support under the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and the possibility to adapt direct payments allocations for calendar year 2027 and Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 as regards more flexible rules on payments of advances in response to the increased fertiliser prices due to the Middle East crisis.
The European Parliament adopted its position at first reading, taking over the Commission's proposal.

To quickly address vulnerabilities of the Union food system resulting from the recent crisis in the Middle East and to assist farmers facing liquidity problems, farmers will be able to receive liquidity support worth up to 80% of the additional fertiliser costs they incur.
Member States will set a maximum amount of support per beneficiary or a maximum number of hectares in respect of which support can be received per beneficiary.
The support will be paid to the farmer by 30 June 2027.

EU countries will also have the possibility to increase advances on direct payments from 70% to 75% and pay them to affected farmers directly after they apply for them (and not only after 16 October as defined by the current rules). Member States may provide additional national financing of up to 200 % of the EAFRD financing allocated in the CAP Strategic Plan.
Member States will also have greater flexibility to adjust their direct payments budgets for the 2027 calendar year.

The European Parliament approved a plan, by 576 votes to 62 with 15 abstentions, that changes two EU farming rules to help farmers hit by higher fertiliser prices caused by the Middle East crisis. Parliament adopted the European Commission's proposal as its own position.

Farmers facing extra fertiliser costs will be able to receive liquidity support, meaning money to help cover cash shortfalls, worth up to 80% of those additional costs. Each EU country will decide a maximum amount of support per farmer, or a maximum number of hectares per farmer that can be counted for support. The money will be paid to farmers by 30 June 2027.

EU countries will also be able to pay advances on direct payments sooner and in a larger share. The advance can rise from 70% to 75%, and it can be paid as soon as the farmer applies, rather than only after 16 October as current rules require.

Countries may add their own national money on top of EU funds for rural development, up to 200% of the rural development funding allocated in their CAP Strategic Plan. They will also have more freedom to adjust their direct payment budgets for the 2027 calendar year.
